name: Giant Scorpion
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Blindsight 60 ft. Passive Perception 9. No listed languages.
appearance: A large tawny arachnid with broad pincers, jointed legs, and an arched tail ending in one curved stinger.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Basic Rules, version 1.0, November 2018 , printed p. 135.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Claw attacks and one Sting attack.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, 5-ft. reach, one target. On a hit, deal 6 (1d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage and grapple the target (escape DC 12). Each claw can grapple one target at a time.
Sting. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, 5-ft. reach, one creature. On a hit, deal 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing damage. The creature also makes a DC 12 Constitution save, taking 22 (4d10) poison damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

name: Giant Sea Horse
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Passive Perception 11. No listed languages or special senses.
appearance: A large fish with a long tubular snout, bony ridges and a curled tail. The portrait shows muted green and ochre plates.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Basic Rules, version 1.0, November 2018 , printed p. 135.
sections.Traits:
Charge. Move at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and hit it with Ram on the same turn to deal another 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must also pass a DC 11 Strength save or fall prone.
Water Breathing. The sea horse breathes only underwater.
sections.Actions: Ram. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, 5-ft. reach, one target. On a hit, deal 4 (1d6 + 1) bludgeoning damage.

name: Giant Shark
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Perception +3. Blindsight 60 ft. Passive Perception 13. No listed languages.
appearance: A 30-ft. shark with a slate-blue back, a pale belly, visible gill slits and rows of triangular teeth.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Basic Rules, version 1.0, November 2018 , printed p. 135.
sections.Traits:
Blood Frenzy. The shark has advantage on melee attack rolls against creatures below their maximum HP.
Water Breathing. The shark breathes only underwater.
